intro-1.text: Picture this. Dixie Road and Mayfield Road is your job. Two roads, crews out every day, the Region watching. It's Monday, seven a.m.

intro-2.text: Over the weekend, the updates piled up. Daily site reports from the field. A schedule that moved. Costs landing in finance. Extra work waiting on the client's sign-off.

intro-3.text: Every one of them matters. None of them talk to each other. And the one question you actually have, are we okay, isn't answered in any of them.

intro-4.text: So you start calling. The project manager, the superintendent, accounting. By Thursday you have an answer. By then, it's already cost you.

meet-1.text: Now imagine you just ask. TaskForce AI goes through every one of those updates for you, and comes back with one page: what's wrong, how bad, and what to do first.

meet-2.text: Every number on it comes straight from your own records.

brief-lead.text: So. Monday, seven a.m. One question.

brief-ask.text: What should I worry about on Dixie this week?

brief-point.text: It starts with the schedule. Dixie is behind, and half of the delays logged on site came from third parties.

brief-verify.text: One page, from the live records, instead of three reports from three departments. Let's pull each thread.

crews-lead.text: Start with the leak nobody reports: crews being paid to wait. Let's ask it.

crews-ask.text: Where are we paying for crews that aren't producing on Dixie?

crews-point.text: Open-cut foremen, two hundred seventy-three standby hours. Open-cut labourers, two hundred sixty-one. And it peaked in July.

crews-verify.text: Three daily reports, D-S-R forty-three, fifty-seven and forty-four, carry the most standby. That's where the conversation with the superintendent starts this week.

cash-ask.text: How much money is the Dixie & Mayfield job owed right now, and what should we chase first?

cash-point.text: Twenty point two nine million dollars is stuck. Almost all of it is work in the ground, not yet approved for billing.

cash-verify.text: First move: put one point eight two million on item C-fifteen b, Granular A, in this month's progress claim.

schedule-lead.text: Now the delays, and which of them belong on a claim.

schedule-ask.text: Which Dixie delays can we bill back to the Region?

schedule-point.text: Three of the six delays logged on site came from third parties. Those are the ones to take to the Region.

schedule-verify.text: An unmarked Bell duct bank, nesting birds, an archaeological find: each one logged by date and report. That's the evidence a claim is built on.

schedule-map.text: And here's where it's happening: Dixie Road, thirteen plus five-twenty to sixteen plus five hundred, and Mayfield Road, thirty-nine plus seven-fourteen to forty-one plus three seventy-six.

dsr-lead.text: Every answer you just saw is only as good as what comes in from site. So here's what a site supervisor says at the end of his day.

dsr-ask.text: I want to fill today's daily site report.

dsr-open.text: The report opens beside the chat. No typing, no dropdowns. He just talks.

fill-1.text: Start a daily report for Dixie Road and Mayfield Road, on the Dixie corridor site. Day shift, Gurpreet Sandhu supervising.

fill-2.text: On the storm sewer we had one open-cut foreman, four open-cut labourers and two pipelayers, ten hours each.

fill-3.text: We ran the 40 tonne excavator and three tri-axle dump trucks, ten hours each.

fill-4.text: On item C-15 a we placed three hundred tonnes.

fill-5.text: We lost two hours waiting for Bell to locate a duct bank at station fourteen plus two-eighty.

fill-5-point.text: Crew, equipment, quantities against the contract item, and the Bell delay, each matched to your real records.

fill-6-point.text: And the form jumps straight to it.

dsr-review.text: That two-hour Bell delay is on the record, at a station, the same day: the paper trail that wins a delay claim. And these hours and quantities feed tomorrow's standby and billing answers.

outro-1.text: Know where a job stands in one minute, not one week. Find idle crews and unbilled work while it's still recoverable. Every delay logged the same day it happens, ready for a claim.

outro-2.text: You don't need more reports. You need fewer steps between the question and the answer.
